source: data/decks.json (placed lists), data/synergy.json, the catalog, docs/archetypes.md, docs/research.md
note: Questions, not findings: a long-legal card that fits a legend's engine by its text, that the legend's winning lists skip and some other legend plays heavily. The evidence is counted; the hypotheses are the usual explanations, checked against the numbers; the answer is hand-written in docs/research.md.

verdicts.skip: Winners are right to skip it

Kai'Sa, Daughter of the Void.doc: spells — the legend's Power is for spells; the list is removal into a spell top end.

Volibear, Relentless Storm.doc: Mighty — the legend ramps on every Mighty unit, Kadregrin draws per Mighty unit.

Jinx, Loose Cannon.doc: discard — Flame Chompers and Jinx, Rebel pay off discarding; the legend wants an empty hand.

Darius, Hand of Noxus.doc: Legion — the legend adds Energy on the second card; Darius, Trifarian grows on it.

Ahri, Nine-Tailed Fox.doc: none — shrink and removal; nothing loops.

Lee Sin, Blind Monk.doc: buffs — the legend buffs a unit every turn; Lee Sin, Centered, Wizened Elder and Stand United pay the buffs off.

Yasuo, Unforgiven.doc: tokens (Spiderlings, each counting the others) — Hidden lets them land together.

Leona, Radiant Dawn.doc: stuns — the legend buffs when you stun; Leona, Zealot gives stunned enemies −8.

Teemo, Swift Scout.doc: facedown — Hidden swarm; the legend re-hides Teemos.

Viktor, Herald of the Arcane.doc: tokens — Recruits from the legend and Viktor, Leader.

Miss Fortune, Bounty Hunter.doc: movement — Ganking from the legend, and Miss Fortune, Captain readies on her first move.

Sett, The Boss.doc: buffs — buff everything, then cash the buffs in.

Annie, Dark Child.doc: none — burn removal on the legend's end-of-turn runes; nothing loops.

Master Yi, Wuju Bladesman.doc: none — tricks around one lone defender; the legend's +2 is a combat bonus, not a loop.

Lux, Lady of Luminosity.doc: spells — the legend pays off every big spell.

Garen, Might of Demacia.doc: winning fights (wide) — the conquest with four units is the payoff; Recruits are the fuel.

Ekko, Boy Who Shattered Time.doc: none — re-buying play effects, which the reader does not read.

Ziggs, Hexplosives Expert.doc: tokens (Bomb gear) — made at battlefields, killed on purpose and remade.

Mordekaiser, Iron Revenant.doc: deaths — every death puts fuel in the trash for the legend's Power.

Orianna, Lady of Clockwork.doc: gear — the legend turns expensive gear into units.

K'Sante, Pride of Nazumah.doc: winning fights — the legend converts Shield into Assault, so the Shield cards are fuel for attacks.

Riven, The Exile.doc: exhaust — Riven, Broken Blade and Reckless Innovator pay off becoming exhausted; attacking, moving and Ki Burst feed them.

Seraphine, Starry-Eyed Songstress.doc: exhaust — the legend exhausts three units to cut a spell's cost; Seraphine, Inspiring draws for it.

Evelynn, Agony's Embrace.doc: facedown — the legend and Evelynn, Consuming pay off playing from face down, and nearly every card is Hidden.

Jarvan IV, Exemplar of Demacia.doc: gear — Deploy gear; the legend converts each one into a move to that battlefield.

Rumble, Mechanized Menace.doc: none — Mech tribe, which the reader does not read.

Lucian, Purifier.doc: gear — Equipment is the investment; the legend turns each one into Assault.

Draven, Glorious Executioner.doc: winning fights — the legend draws for every combat won.

Rek'Sai, Void Burrower.doc: reveal — the top of the deck. Conquer, flip two, play one: the legend on conquest,

Ornn, Fire Below the Mountain.doc: gear — twenty gear; the legend's Power, Pit Crew and Ornn, Forge God pay them off.

Jax, Grandmaster at Arms.doc: gear — Equipment is the investment; the legend moves it to a fresh carrier.

Irelia, Blade Dancer.doc: ready → move → draw (Herder). Her idea page's Engines panel lists the Radiance

Azir, Emperor of the Sands.doc: tokens from gear — Equipment makes Sand Soldiers, and Arise! makes one per Equipment.

Ezreal, Prodigal Explorer.doc: none — answers that choose twice draw a card; removal, not a loop.

Renata Glasc, Chem-Baroness.doc: none — Gold, which is mana, not an engine.

Sivir, Battle Mistress.doc: none — a fast combat curve; Gold and Ganking are not patterns the reader knows.

Fiora, Grand Duelist.doc: Mighty — the legend ramps whenever a unit becomes Mighty; Fiora, Victorious gains her keywords while Mighty.

Jhin, Virtuoso.doc: spells — four 4+ spells banished to the legend.

Rengar, Pridestalker.doc: winning fights — the legend pumps a unit for every unit you play, and Ambush puts them into the fight.

Pyke, Bloodharbor Ripper.doc: none — bounce and replay for Gold.

Vi, Piltover Enforcer.doc: gear and winning fights — Equipment with Assault and Ganking; the legend readies on big conquests.

Lillia, Bashful Bloom.doc: tokens — the legend makes Sprites, cheaper for each Temporary unit you have.

Master Yi, Wuju Master.doc: XP — Hunt cards and conquests feed it; the legend's Level 6 and Level 11 are what it buys.

Vex, Gloomist.doc: none — Vex, Apathetic's stun lock and removal buy time; Steel Paws empowering itself is not a loop.

Ivern, Green Father.doc: none — tribe tags, which the reader does not read.

Diana, Scorn of the Moon.doc: spells — showdown spells on the legend's showdown-only Energy.

LeBlanc, Deceiver.doc: deaths — Deathknell units and Karthus doubling them; the legend's Temporary copy dies and triggers again.

Kha'Zix, Voidreaver.doc: movement — in to win the fight, out before the retake. Won fights pay the XP that

Poppy, Keeper of the Hammer.doc: XP — from holds and Demacian Diplomat, spent to draw, buff and discount Poppy.

Akali, Rogue Assassin.doc: movement — Akali, Deadly Weapon and Akali, Silent pay off moving; the legend pulls units home to move again.

Renekton, Butcher of the Sands.doc: none — a unit-ramp curve: the legend's Energy is for units, and nothing loops.

Zed, Master of Shadows.doc: tokens (Shadow Clones) — Zed swaps places with them.

Nasus, Curator of the Sands.doc: none — big-spell ramp: the legend readies runes for 7+ costs, and nothing loops.

Shen, Eye of Twilight.doc: none — pair defence; it wins by holding, not by a loop.

Jayce, Defender of Tomorrow.doc: gear — ramp gear the legend readies, into the top end and Gutter Palace.

Mel, Soul's Reflection.doc: Empower and spells — Applied Researchers and Shock Blast are cheaper while something is Empowered.

Ambessa, Matriarch of War.doc: Empower — the legend empowers itself whenever you empower something else, and spends it to ready a unit; the list is Empower cards.

Kennen, Heart of the Tempest.doc: plays from elsewhere — the legend converts each one into Assault; Flow, Fizz and Matriarch feed it.

items.title: Why do Kennen, Heart of the Tempest's winners skip 2 Movement cards?
evidence: 75 placed lists. Plays from elsewhere > Movement > Trash size > Empower > Facedown, strongest first.
hypotheses: Movement is this deck's #2 engine; its main one is Plays from elsewhere. Its cards here may be insurance, not a plan.
A payoff is worth what it multiplies: here 3 Traveling Merchant, 3 Shadow Order Disciple, 2 Ride the Wind, 1 Flash, 1 Tideturner.
The winning list averages 2.8 Energy with 22 of 40 cards at 2 or less; the most-asked Power is Chaos 20, Order 1.
New cards add 7 to Movement in these colours (Satchel Charge, Siren of the Shallows, Demon Shade, Lulu, Whimsical, …); an old reason may not hold.

cards.answer: As the engine answer, and smaller still: Karthus doubles what Rek'Sai's Deathknells give — a 1-Might Bird, an exhausted Gold, two Recruits once Empowered — for 3 Energy and the deck's scarcest Power (Order). It is a 3-Might body that does nothing on the turn it is played, in a deck that wins by having more bodies at more battlefields than the opponent can answer. Doubling Ruined Rex (LeBlanc) is a different card. The discovery report's first lead was this card, and it was wrong. Whether it stacks with Detonation Amplifier is also unsettled by the rules (only Repeat stacks, §820.3) — a second reason not to build around it.

items.answer: Rek'Sai's engine is the top of the deck, not deaths: conquer, reveal two, play one, with Breacher's Accelerate and Undertitan's [Add] 2 paying off what arrives that way. The deck is cheap bodies so that almost anything it flips is playable (27 of 40 cards at 2 Energy or less), and its Deathknell units are insurance that makes a lost fight cheap (guides/reksai-void-burrower.md §6). The payoffs add little when flipped or when they fight: the 3-Energy ones (Karthus, Black Rose Dignitary, Loyal Poro) would take the slot of Faithful Manufactor and Breacher, the 2-Energy ones (Soaring Scout, Unsung Hero) that of Inferna and the Deathknell bodies they would pay off, and the Order payoffs compete for the Order Power that Undertitan, Vanguard Captain and Cull the Weak already ask for. LeBlanc plays these cards because LeBlanc's deck is the Deathknell deck; Rek'Sai's winners, 0 of 61, are right not to.
